items.headline: Stocks ended nearly flat as bank earnings gave mixed signals
items.note: S&P 500 −0.02%, Nasdaq about −0.15%, Dow −0.35% on Tuesday. Goldman Sachs beat profit estimates (EPS $17.01 vs. about $13 expected) while JPMorgan missed ($5.57 vs. $5.90), and Wells Fargo fell about 3%.

items.headline: Memory-chip stocks dragged on the Nasdaq
items.note: Memory makers sold off, helping pull the Nasdaq lower. High-bandwidth memory is a key part of AI hardware, so chip swings are worth watching for AI-related jobs.

items.headline: September inflation (CPI) report is due today, with the Fed meeting Oct 27–28
items.note: Previews expect core inflation to keep slowing, and markets mostly expect the Fed to hold at its late-October meeting. A hot number could revive talk of another hike, which would pressure tech stocks and startup hiring.

items.headline: Anthropic reportedly meets institutional investors today as it moves toward an IPO
items.note: Bloomberg reportedly said investors were invited to Anthropic's San Francisco HQ on Oct 14. This is a secondhand report, but a possible AI-lab IPO would be a big event for the AI job market.

items.headline: Data science hiring looks steady, not booming
items.note: One analysis of US postings finds a steady flow, mostly mid-level or senior roles, with New York holding about 14% of postings. Python (82%) and SQL (55%) lead the skills; this is a recruiting-firm analysis, so treat it as indicative.

learn.explain: Inflation is the rate at which prices rise over time, so each dollar buys a little less. The Consumer Price Index (CPI) tracks it by pricing a fixed basket of everyday things (food, rent, gas, clothes) each month and comparing with a year earlier. "Core" CPI leaves out food and energy because they swing a lot, so it shows the underlying trend. The Fed watches inflation closely: if it stays too high, the Fed can raise interest rates to cool spending. That is why a CPI release can move stocks the same day.
learn.try: Look up the latest CPI release on bls.gov and find the difference between the headline and core numbers.
